To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the subcellular energetic state of a cell or tissue is a function of its metabolic state, and (2) the subcellularenergetic state of a tissue is a function not only of its metabolic state but also of its oxygenation status.

(1) the mitochondria are capable of adapting to a wide variety of adverse environmental conditions, (2) these adaptations are not unique to cancer cells and preimplantation mammalian embryos, and (3) these adaptations can be exploited therapeutically in humans.

(1) the mitochondrial respiratory chain is capable of generating ATP under hypoxic conditions, (2) mitochondrial ROS are generated in response to hypoxia and oxidative stress, (3) mitochondria are capable of responding to oxidative stress through the upregulation of antioxidant defense systems (eg, glutathione, thioredoxin), and (4) mitochondria are also capable of responding to hypoxia through the upregu- lation of glycolytic enzymes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying common themes and principles that underlie seemingly disparate phenomena.
understanding how the cell and the organism respond to stress.
the ability of organisms to survive, and even thrive, in ostensibly adverse environments, and we are interested in the commonalities that exist across species.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the mitochondrial dysfunction observed during sepsis is complex and likely involves multiple mechanisms, and the precise nature of the dysfunction may depend on the specific pathogen and the stage of sepsis.
the impact of septic injury on the mitochondria and the role of mitochondrial dysfunction in the pathophysiology of sepsis are not yet known.
the impact of septic shock on mitochondrial function, including the role of mitochondrial biogenesis and the role of mitochondrial antioxidant systems, is not fully understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sepsis is a complex disease with multiple organ systems involved and that the mitochondria is one of many potential targets for therapy.
the mitochondrial respiratory chain is an important source of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and that the mitochondria are a key target of ROS in sepsis and other conditions of oxidative stress.
, in the context of the current article, sepsis is a complex, multifactorial disease that can impact mitochondrial structure and function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are a number of common themes that emerge when considering subcellular energetic processes in the face of oxidative and/or hypoxic stress.
, in addition to the well-known effects of hypoxia on the mitochondria, oxidative stress also has a profound impact on the mitochondria and its bioenergetics.
, although there may be differences between species, the fundamental processes of life are remarkably similar.
